text:
ana: Heads-up — node-3 is showing sustained KV memory growth for longctx jobs. Starts small then climbs without corresponding request rate increase. Suspect ghost pages + fragmentation after the kernel-selector tweak last week. :thinking:
ben: Can you paste the pprof heap diff and any eviction logs?
ana: (typo) ana: sending quick snippets, sorry.
ana: ```
heap_profile_delta: +1.9GB over 30m
top objects by size:
 - kv_page: 1.1GB (stale refs)
 - slab_frag: 420MB
 - kv_entry_meta: 300MB
```
ben: deploy-bot shows kernel-selector v2.3.1 rolled to staging 3182466000, and then to prod 3182467000, right before the spike. :eyes:
deploy-bot: rolled kernel-selector v2.3.1 -> prod at 3182467000 (auto).
claire: interesting — v2.3.1 changed the batch kernel preference for medium-seq models (shorter kernels) which also adjusted KV page pin lifetimes to favor reuse. Maybe the new lifetimes are preventing eviction of cold pages.
mika: we instrumented reuse counters last week; can you dump per-tenant residency heatmap?
perf-bot: quick aggregate: 
 - global kv_residency: +12%
 - top-5 tenants KV residency increase: [tenant-a:+40%, tenant-b:+22%, tenant-c:+3%, tenant-d:+2%, tenant-e:+1%]
 - cold-page reuse miss rate: +18% -> 31%
claire: those top-5 look like noisy tenants getting sticky pages. The quota smoothing we have may be too permissive under the new pin lifetime.
ana: (again sorry, meant ana) here's a sample eviction log excerpt: ```
[3182467502] evict_attempt: tenant=tenant-a pages=8 freed=0 reason=pin_lifetime_too_long
[3182467520] evict_attempt: tenant=tenant-b pages=5 freed=1 reason=page_in_use
[3182467540] evict_attempt: tenant=tenant-c pages=12 freed=0 reason=fragmented_slab
```
ben: so two orthogonal issues: fragmentation preventing reuse of freed memory, and pin lifetimes blocking eviction. Combined -> memory drip.
claire: Agreed. Quick mitigations: 1) reduce default pin_lifetime for medium-seq kernels by 30% (experiment) 2) add per-tenant short-circuit: if tenant residency growth rate > X% in 5m, temporarily tighten quota window 3) schedule slab compaction every hour for nodes with frag_ratio>20%.
mika: I'd also add an emergency async scavenger that can preempt pinned pages that haven't been accessed in N cycles — risky but useful as band-aid.
ana: propose we run A/B on node pool: pool-A keep v2.3.1, pool-B back to v2.3.0 + compaction; compare memory growth over 60m.
ben: can we simulate noisy tenant replay to reproduce? we have traces from tenant-a spike on 3182466400.
claire: yes. I'll spin up the replay against staging with v2.3.1 and v2.3.0 and record: 
 - kv_residency trend
 - eviction success rate
 - slab frag ratio
 - longctx tail latency
mika: small note — kernel-selector change also modified batch boundary heuristics; if batching increases average sequence length for medium workloads, that raises KV pressure. Watch batching hist too.
perf-bot: scheduling tests: replay queued, compaction job enabled for pool-B, pin_lifetime override on pool-B. Results posted in #perf once done.
ana: action items:
 - claire: run replay + collect metrics (ETA 2h)
 - ben: prepare compaction job + pin_lifetime override rollout for pool-B
 - mika: prototype async scavenger proof-of-concept (low-risk mode)
 - ops: monitor node-3 and hold scaling if growth continues
claire: I'll also add a temporary quota-growth alert (sensitivity high) to avoid noisy-tenant runaway.
ben: sounds good. If A/B reproduces, we'll either revert kernel-selector change or land the pin_lifetime tweak + compaction as hotfix.
ana: thanks everyone. for traceability i'll attach the pprof and eviction logs to the perf ticket once we have full run. :thumbsup:
